## What counts as oranges

<a id="hmi-ing-001"></a>
<a id="what-commodity-biological-species-edible-part-and-commercial-forms-does-this-page-cover"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-002"></a>
<a id="which-processing-states-and-derivatives-are-distinct-materials-rather-than-synonyms"></a>

<div class="hmi-analyte-explorer" id="hmi-occurrence-oranges" data-analyte-explorer data-compact-intro="true" data-source-summaries="true"><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure" data-explorer-context><summary data-open-context aria-haspopup="dialog" aria-controls="hmi-occurrence-oranges-drawer">Comparison methods and scope</summary><div data-explorer-context-content>

<p>Each row is one statistic a source reports for one form of oranges, group and metal; percentiles, ranges and maxima reported for the same samples as a mean or median are shown on that row. Different forms and preparation states are kept apart, and dry-weight results never share a reference with as-sold or fresh-weight results. Ratings place a result against an HMI reference built from monitoring results and ordinary-setting medians for the same form and basis. Same-study contrasts compare a contaminated or treated site with its control, targeted with random sampling, a prepared form with the unprocessed one, or one group of a study with the median of its other groups. Held rows failed a check against their own source and are shown but not compared.</p>

Other forms, other bases, targeted sampling and results from mining, industrial, wastewater-affected, experimental, fertiliser or manufacturer settings are kept out of this reference.</p><p>Inverse weighted empirical CDF; midpoint at exact cumulative-weight boundaries. At least four reference units and a definitely positive Q1 to Q3 spread are required. This is a display eligibility rule, not statistical validation.</p><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Limitations</p><p>6 sampling families with different designs; none is a probability sample of world supply. <a id="sources-and-contamination-pathways"></a>
## How metals reach oranges

<a id="hmi-ing-010"></a>
<a id="what-evidence-supports-root-uptake-surface-deposition-feed-transfer-or-other-biological-pathways"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-011"></a>
<a id="what-contamination-can-arise-from-agricultural-inputs-harvesting-processing-equipment-or-packaging"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-012"></a>
<a id="which-source-attribution-claims-are-measured-modelled-inferred-or-unresolved"></a>

The evidence on how metals reach oranges comes from studies that compared exposed and ordinary settings. Oranges, as sold from migratable fraction in 0.07 M HCl had Ba higher at 7,900 µg/kg, against 1,200 µg/kg for migratable fraction in 0.07 M HCl in the same study.<sup class="cite">[[sources/turner2018-secondhand-plastic-toys|7]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Andrew Turner · 2018</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/turner2018-secondhand-plastic-toys">Concentrations and Migratabilities of Hazardous Elements in Second-Hand Children&#39;s Plastic toys</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Environmental Science &amp; Technology 52(5):3110-3116</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/turner2018-secondhand-plastic-toys">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

These are observational comparisons from single studies; the size of the difference depends on the site, metal and distance.

Thesis, Sher-e-Bangla Agricultural University, Dhaka</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/afrin2020-heavy-metals-fruits-dhaka">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> In another study, lead across 5 groups of oranges ranged from 40 µg/kg (Oyingbo market (Lagos Mainland)) to 217 µg/kg (Ketu market (Ikosi/Isheri)); the lowest is the lowest observed in that study, not an established sourcing preference.<sup class="cite">[[sources/rotimi2018-lagos-market-fruits-metals|19]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Rotimi OT, Ogunyebi AL, Fingesi TS · 2018</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/rotimi2018-lagos-market-fruits-metals">Evaluation of Heavy Metals Level and Proximate Analysis of Common Fruits from Selected Markets in Lagos, Nigeria</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Journal of Applied Sciences and Environmental Management, Vol. 22 (5) 791-795</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/rotimi2018-lagos-market-fruits-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

## Trade-offs and limits of controls

<a id="hmi-ing-022"></a>

<a id="hmi-ing-024"></a>
<a id="what-costs-constraints-adverse-effects-or-failure-modes-are-documented-and-which-are-unknown"></a>

Avoiding exposed growing areas lowered the metal measured in the studies available, but no study measured the cost or supply effect of doing so.<sup class="cite">[[sources/turner2018-secondhand-plastic-toys|7]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Andrew Turner · 2018</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/turner2018-secondhand-plastic-toys">Concentrations and Migratabilities of Hazardous Elements in Second-Hand Children&#39;s Plastic toys</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Environmental Science &amp; Technology 52(5):3110-3116</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/turner2018-secondhand-plastic-toys">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Metals do not move together, so a lot that passes a lead limit says little about cadmium, arsenic or nickel unless those are tested as well.

Results depend on the method and its reporting limit. Reporting limits for lead ranged from 0.333 µg/kg (WHO GEMS/Food) to 4,000 µg/kg (WHO GEMS/Food), so a non-detect from a less sensitive method says much less.<sup ## Oranges FAQs

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="what-heavy-metals-are-found-in-oranges" data-anchor="what-heavy-metals-are-found-in-oranges" data-question="What heavy metals are found in oranges?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>What heavy metals are found in oranges?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

The library reports lead, cadmium, total arsenic, inorganic arsenic, total mercury, methylmercury, nickel, chromium, aluminium, tin, antimony, uranium, Co, Cu, Fe, Mn, Zn, V, Se, As, Ba, Hg, Mo and Tl in oranges, most often lead, cadmium and total arsenic.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span <details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="how-do-heavy-metals-get-into-oranges" data-anchor="how-do-heavy-metals-get-into-oranges" data-question="How do heavy metals get into oranges?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>How do heavy metals get into oranges?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

In the studies available, oranges from contaminated or exposed settings carried more metal than oranges from the same study’s control.<sup class="cite">[[sources/turner2018-secondhand-plastic-toys|7]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Andrew Turner · 2018</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/turner2018-secondhand-plastic-toys">Concentrations and Migratabilities of Hazardous Elements in Second-Hand Children&#39;s Plastic toys</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Environmental Science &amp; Technology 52(5):3110-3116</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/turner2018-secondhand-plastic-toys">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Oranges, as sold from migratable fraction in 0.07 M HCl had Ba higher at 7,900 µg/kg, against 1,200 µg/kg for migratable fraction in 0.07 M HCl in the same study.<sup class="cite">[[sources/turner2018-secondhand-plastic-toys|7]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Andrew Turner · 2018</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/turner2018-secondhand-plastic-toys">Concentrations and Migratabilities of Hazardous Elements in Second-Hand Children&#39;s Plastic toys</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Environmental Science &amp; Technology 52(5):3110-3116</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/turner2018-secondhand-plastic-toys">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="which-regions-report-the-lowest-levels-in-oranges" data-anchor="which-regions-report-the-lowest-levels-in-oranges" data-question="Which regions report the lowest levels in oranges?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Which regions report the lowest levels in oranges?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Among GEMS/Food reporting regions, oranges, as sold had the lowest lead subgroup median in PAHO (10.4 µg/kg) and the highest in EURO (215 µg/kg); reporting regions are markets, not growing areas.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> For total arsenic, the lowest regional median was in EURO (0.307 µg/kg) and the highest in EURO (22 µg/kg).<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>
